title: Jeff's Farm (Chas McIvor)
style: Afro-folk acoustic guitar Zimbabwe farm portrait warm baritone male vocal storytelling 100bpm brushed drums walking bass wide open landscape sound honest working man character portrait
lyrics:
[Intro - acoustic guitar, open and wide, slow sunrise feel]
Before the paperwork, before the visa
Before Australia knew the name
There was a farm in Zimbabwe
And a man who ran it straight

[Verse 1]
Jeff was up before the light came over
He walked the rows before the workers arrived
Not because he didn't trust them
But because that's what a farming man does in his life
And when he spoke, they listened
Not from fear but from respect earned slow
The kind of man you work hard for
Because you know he knows what you know

[Verse 2]
Jill ran the dairy with a different kind of certainty
The morning shift, the evening round
The cows don't lie, the milk won't wait for anyone
And she kept it coming without a sound
Between the two of them they held a world together
Red dust mornings, cool nights, that high African sky
And the farm breathed in and the farm breathed out
And everything happened exactly right

[Chorus]
Jeff's farm
Where the workers came back every morning
Jeff's farm
Where respect was a thing you earned and kept
Jeff's farm
Where the red dust tells no stories
That the people there already know
Jeff's farm
That is where the family starts to grow

[Bridge - spoken, level and warm]
They left the farm.
That's a hard sentence.
But they brought it with them.
You always do.
You bring the way you walk the rows at sunrise.
You bring the way you know when something's right.
You bring Jeff's farm.
Even in Australia.
Even now.

[Outro - guitar alone, unhurried]
Jeff's farm
Still somewhere in how they carry themselves
Jeff's farm
Jill's dairy in the early morning hours
Jeff's farm
In how Joel knows what a good man looks like
Jeff's farm
In everything Kerri is
